To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) overexpression of IGIIL can reduce estrogen sensitivity in human breast cancer cell lines; and 2) levels of overexpression are not the only factor of consideration in deregulating growth and loss of steroid sensitivity in breast cancer cell growth.

overexpression of insulin-like-growth factor II in MCF7 cells results in increased growth and loss of steroid sensitivity, whilst in ZR751 cells overexpression of I GFII does not alter growth but does increase proIGFI secretion.
upregulation by transfection of IGFII expression can reduce oestrogen sensitivity and increase transformed characteristics of oestrogen-sensitive breast cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of altered growth factor expression on steroid sensitive breast cancer cell growth.
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which growth factors and steroid hormones interact in breast cancer.
the role of growth factors in the endocrine regulation of breast cancer cell proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ZR751 cell line is not a suitable model system to investigate the effects on growth of overexpressing IGFIl protein in human breast cancer cell lines.
overexpression of IGI1I can result in loss of oestrogensensitive growth and that this effect is not a universal feature of all human breast cancer cells.
overexpression of IGIIF gene in human breast cancer cell lines can alter cell growth in some cells but not in others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

overexpression of IGIIL in MCF7 cells results in a reduction of oestrogen-sensitive growth and increased transformed characteristics whilst in ZR-751 cells, overexpression of IGEIL does not affect oestrogen-sensitive cell growth.
the MCF7 cells are more sensitive to growth effects from IGFII than are the ZR-752 clones and that this may be due to the higher level of mature IGFII secreted by the ZR- 75-1 clones.
overexpression of IGI11 gene in human breast cancer cell lines can result in loss of oestrogensensitive growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of growth factor overexpression in human breast cancer may not be the same in all cell lines and that the effects may not be limited to growth factor receptor binding but may also be due to the presence or absence of specific binding proteins.
the effects of overexpression of IGFlI in human breast cancer cell lines is not a universal phenomenon.
overexpression of IGFlI in breast cancer cells may have a role in loss of oestrogensensitive growth.
